summary: Modern data platforms have rapidly embedded AI/ML directly into the database layer, with vector search, in-database model inference, and LLM integration becoming standard competitive differentiators by 2026. Research indicates that 75% of enterprise AI applications will depend on vector search capabilities, and vector database adoption grew 377% year over year — the fastest growth among all LLM-related technologies. Cloud data warehouses (Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML) now offer agentic and generative AI features natively, while operational databases increasingly add native or extension-based vector indexing to power retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workloads.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Cortex AI, Snowflake Intelligence, AI CoWork, Adaptive Compute
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex provides fully managed LLM functions (summarization, translation, sentiment, completion), Cortex Search, and Cortex Analyst for natural-language querying. In 2026 Snowflake pushed further into agentic AI: Snowflake Intelligence crossed 2,500 accounts within three months (reported May 2026), and AI CoWork plus Adaptive Compute reached general availability in June 2026. Snowflake reported more than 9,100 Cortex AI accounts as of January 2026. Snowflake also made data 'AI-ready by design' with Snowflake Postgres running natively in the AI Data Cloud (announced February 2026), which includes Apache AGE graph support.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake Cortex provides built-in VECTOR data type and vector similarity functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, etc.), and Cortex Search offers a managed hybrid vector + keyword retrieval service. Snowflake Postgres also adds pgvector-style vector capabilities within the AI Data Cloud.
databases.llm_integration: Deeply integrated — hosted foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) accessible via SQL/Python functions; Cortex Analyst and Snowflake Intelligence enable agentic natural-language analytics.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM functions billed per token processed, Cortex Search billed on serving + indexing compute. Adaptive Compute (GA June 2026) aims to optimize warehouse sizing automatically.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML, Vertex AI integration, generative AI SQL functions
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create and run machine learning models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization) using standard SQL, with no data movement. It integrates with Vertex AI to call hosted Gemini and other foundation models via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and supports remote model inference and AutoML. BigQuery also provides AI-driven features such as text generation, embeddings, and now agentic/analytics assistance.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports vector embeddings storage and the VECTOR_SEARCH function with native vector indexes (IVF and brute-force), enabling similarity search directly in SQL without an external vector store.
databases.llm_integration: Strong — Vertex AI remote models (Gemini family, PaLM, embeddings APIs) callable directly from BigQuery SQL; integrates with Gemini in BigQuery for assisted query authoring.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery on-demand (per TB scanned) or capacity-based (slots) pricing; ML.GENERATE functions incur Vertex AI model usage charges on top of BigQuery compute. Vector index creation/storage adds costs.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities primarily through extensions. pgvector adds a vector data type with exact and approximate nearest-neighbor search (IVFFlat and HNSW indexes). The pgai extension (from Timescale) brings embedding generation and LLM calls directly into SQL, and pgvectorscale improves vector index performance at scale. These make standard Postgres a popular, cost-effective RAG backend.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL — vector search is provided via the pgvector extension (with HNSW/IVFFlat indexing). Capable and widely adopted, but it is an extension rather than a built-in engine feature.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension, PostgreSQL can generate embeddings and invoke LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, etc.) directly from SQL; otherwise integration is handled in the application layer.
databases.pricing_notes: Core PostgreSQL and pgvector/pgai are free and open-source; costs depend on self-hosting or managed provider (RDS, Aurora, Supabase, Timescale/Tiger Cloud). External LLM API calls incur provider charges.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using SQL by integrating Aurora (MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible) with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock. Developers call ML models directly from SQL functions for inference (fraud detection, sentiment, recommendations, and generative AI via Bedrock) without building separate inference pipelines.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Aurora PostgreSQL supports vector search only through the pgvector extension; there is no proprietary built-in vector engine, so vector_search is marked false per the native-only criterion.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI/LLM inference and embeddings callable from SQL, and with SageMaker for custom models.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora charges for database instances/storage/I-O; ML inference adds SageMaker endpoint or Bedrock model invocation costs separately. Aurora Serverless v2 available for variable workloads.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Redshift ML enables data analysts and scientists to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL CREATE MODEL commands, leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. It supports in-database prediction, bring-your-own-model, and generative AI via Amazon Bedrock LLM integration for use cases on warehouse-scale data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native in the data-warehouse engine in the traditional sense — Redshift supports a VECTOR/embedding workflow mainly through Bedrock integration and does not offer a mature built-in ANN vector index comparable to BigQuery or Snowflake; marked false. Vector workloads are typically offloaded to OpenSearch or Aurora/pgvector.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock (generative AI, embeddings) and SageMaker, callable from SQL for inference and text generation.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift provisioned (RA3 nodes) or Serverless (RPU-based) pricing; ML model training uses SageMaker resources and generative calls use Bedrock, billed separately.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) + Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides an end-to-end platform for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing ML and generative AI models, including Foundation Model APIs, Model Serving, Agent Framework, and MLflow integration. Databricks Vector Search provides a managed vector database tightly integrated with Unity Catalog governance and Delta tables, with automatic embedding sync.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in, fully managed vector index service (with Delta Sync indexes that auto-update from source tables) integrated with Unity Catalog and Mosaic AI retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Extensive — Foundation Model APIs host and serve open and proprietary LLMs (Llama, DBRX, Claude via partnerships), plus fine-tuning, RAG agents, and external model gateways through Mosaic AI.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search and Model Serving billed on compute/serving endpoints, Foundation Model APIs on pay-per-token or provisioned throughput.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search + Atlas AI integrations
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and performing semantic/similarity search with approximate nearest-neighbor indexing, supporting hybrid search that combines vector, full-text, and metadata filtering in a single query. It is designed to power RAG and AI applications directly on operational data without a separate vector store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in capability of MongoDB Atlas using HNSW-based approximate nearest-neighbor indexing ($vectorSearch aggregation stage), natively integrated with the document database.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face, AWS Bedrock) and popular frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) for RAG; embedding generation handled externally or via integrations.
databases.pricing_notes: Part of MongoDB Atlas; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes (separately scalable, billed by instance size/time) on top of cluster costs. Available on Atlas dedicated tiers.
